title: Is relevance enough to knock?
question: When a retained conflict becomes relevant to a new turn, how can Turtle notice that relevance without treating relevance itself as permission to resurface the conflict?
why_now: Conflict Explanation now has a standing regression for how competing rules are framed. Neutral framing is still incomplete if machine-detected relevance can decide when old material re-enters the learner's foreground.
possible_possibles: A learner-authored resurfacing watchpoint that names when a retained conflict may return.
A quiet dormant marker the learner can pull into view without Turtle pushing it forward.
A machine relevance proposal that stays internal until an explicit learner-controlled surfacing gate authorizes display.
x_factor: whoooo knooooowwwssssssssssss — maybe the best continuity cue is a tiny pull-tab the learner can choose, not Turtle deciding that relevance deserves a knock.
constraints: Relevance is evidence for noticing, not authority to resurface.
Preserve rule authorship, scope, and provenance.
Do not introduce generalized persistent personal memory.
Do not infer human availability or desire to revisit old material.
Machine proposals remain reversible and have no production authority.

ontology_mappings.rationale: The learner retains authority over foreground return.
Machine salience must not narrow the next move.
A return may alter the joint trajectory while the human gate remains authoritative.
Quiet retention preserves future paths without forcing one now.
Any return must preserve why the conflict exists and who authored it.

ctc_mappings.rationale: Learner purpose governs whether old conflict returns.
A prior unresolved problem may stay available without becoming compulsory.

ctc_mappings.domain: Technology as Tool to Think With
ctc_mappings.rationale: Relevance is material for inspection rather than an action command.
Learners may deliberately revisit prior conflict.

uncaptured_residue.observation: The framework does not yet distinguish useful relevance detection from salience pressure as a first-class analytic object.
Structural tests cannot establish whether a learner experiences resurfacing as respectful or intrusive.
